naamp.robustness: small effect; >=8-stop sensitivity passes, complete-10-stop sensitivity narrowly crosses zero

frogid.design: independent expert-validated short call recordings, conditional on >=1 calling species
frogid.robustness: weather-cell and recorder clustering both pass

supported_claim: Across two independent acoustic monitoring systems, more recent rainfall is associated with greater short-window overlap in frog calling activity across species.
strengthened_interpretation: The FrogID validation is conditional on at least one species already calling, so the replicated rain association cannot be explained solely by rainfall increasing the probability that any frog is acoustically active.
not_supported: rain-driven pairwise co-calling network densification in NAAMP

temperature.note: positive temperature association survives plausibility QC and source-scale stratification, but it has not been independently validated here

mechanistic_boundary: Results support event-level community synchrony/shared environmental activation, not causal interspecific facilitation or pairwise network rewiring.
reason_no_meta_analysis: NAAMP and FrogID use different sampling units, observation designs, and rainfall measurements.
